intervention_dose: doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + trabectedin 1.1 mg/m2 IV q3w x6, then trabectedin maintenance to progression; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w x6
indication: metastatic or unresectable uterine or soft-tissue leiomyosarcoma, chemotherapy-naive
population_detail: ECOG 0-1 required; 67 of 150 patients (45%) had uterine LMS; randomization stratified by uterine vs soft-tissue origin; surgery for residual disease allowed after 6 cycles in both arms
design: randomized open-label phase 3 (French Sarcoma Group, 20 centres), BICR-assessed primary endpoint
safety_summary: Combination is substantially more myelotoxic than doxorubicin alone: G3-4 neutropenia 80% vs 13%, thrombocytopenia 47% vs 0%, febrile neutropenia 28% vs 9%. One treatment-related death, in the doxorubicin-alone arm (cardiac failure).

toxicities.notes: the one treatment-related death occurred in the doxorubicin-alone arm (1/75)

notes: Primary report of the regimen she is about to start; pivotal for the LMS-04 strategy. The PMID a search commonly surfaces, 36174625, is a letter about this trial, not the trial. Per-term G3-4 rates above are from the combination phase; maintenance-phase safety detail sits behind the paywall (no PMC; CT.gov NCT02997358 has no posted results).

intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04) — final OS
intervention_dose: as in primary report; trabectedin maintenance continued to progression
indication: metastatic or unresectable uterine or soft-tissue leiomyosarcoma, chemotherapy-naive
population_detail: same 150-patient ITT population as the 2022 primary report; analyses adjusted for uterine vs soft-tissue origin and disease stage
design: final overall-survival analysis of the randomized phase 3 LMS-04 trial (median follow-up 55 months)

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: adjusted HR for death; 107 of 150 patients had died

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: adjusted HR, updated at final analysis

safety_summary: Abstract reports only that adverse events and dose reductions were more frequent with doxorubicin-trabectedin; per-term combination-phase rates are on the 2022 primary-report row.
notes: This is the OS readout that turns LMS-04 from a PFS result into a survival benefit, and the main reason the regimen was chosen for her. Toxicities left empty after the full fallback chain failed: abstract has no per-term data, NEJM has no PMC deposit, CT.gov NCT02997358 hasResults=false, publisher page returns 403.

intervention_dose: doxorubicin 25 mg/m2/day d1-3 + ifosfamide 10 g/m2 over 4 days with mesna and pegfilgrastim q3w; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w
indication: advanced or metastatic high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma, first line
population_detail: age 18-60, WHO PS 0-1; all histologies of high-grade STS, not LMS-specific
design: randomized controlled phase 3 (EORTC 62012), OS primary endpoint
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 14.3 vs 12.8 mo; mPFS 7.4 vs 4.6 mo
safety_summary: Intensified combination roughly doubles to quadruples high-grade hematologic toxicity vs doxorubicin alone; febrile neutropenia 46% vs 13% despite pegfilgrastim.
notes: The trial behind the rule that combination cytotoxics buy response and PFS but not OS in aggregate STS; the age band (18-60) matches her. Pooled STS, not uLMS-specific, so it is weaker evidence for her than LMS-04, which reversed the OS conclusion in histology-selected LMS.

intervention_dose: gemcitabine 675 mg/m2 d1,8 + docetaxel 75 mg/m2 d8 q3w x6; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w x6
indication: previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma
population_detail: LMS-enriched: 118/257 (46%) leiomyosarcoma, of whom 71 (28% of trial) uterine LMS; Trojani grade 2-3
design: randomized controlled phase 3 (GeDDiS, ISRCTN07742377), 24-week PFS-rate primary endpoint

outcomes.name: PFS
outcomes.variance_or_ci: 95% CI 18.1-20.0 as printed (upper bound is an apparent typographical error in the published abstract)

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: gem-doce arm; vs 76.3 wk doxorubicin; HR 1.14, p=0.41 (full text)

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: no differential treatment effect by histology; uLMS-specific PFS not separately reported

safety_summary: Different toxicity trade: doxorubicin gave more neutropenia, febrile neutropenia and mucositis; gem-doce more fatigue. No treatment-related deaths reported.
notes: The head-to-head that keeps anthracycline first: gem-doce showed no superiority even in an LMS-enriched population, including the uterine subset (interaction p=0.38). Its practical role for her is first-line fallback if baseline LVEF or pulmonary reserve at 8,500 ft rules out doxorubicin.

intervention_dose: gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 d1,8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 d8 q3w with G-CSF d9-15; 25% dose reduction after prior pelvic RT
indication: unresectable leiomyosarcoma (29/34 uterine), 0-2 prior regimens

outcomes.notes: 3 CR + 15 PR of 34; 50% of doxorubicin-pretreated patients responded

safety_summary: Myelosuppression frequent but febrile neutropenia rare (6%) with G-CSF support; no bleeding events.
notes: The 53% ORR that made gem-doce a uLMS standard is from 34 patients at one centre with mixed lines of therapy; the GOG first-line trial (PMID 18534250) halved that estimate. Read the two together before quoting a response rate.

intervention_dose: gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 over 90 min d1,8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 d8 q3w with G-CSF d9; lower doses after prior pelvic RT

population_detail: uLMS only; first-line; multicentre cooperative-group setting

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: CR 4.8%, PR 31%; SD in a further 26.2%

safety_summary: Myelosuppression was the major toxicity; one possibly-related grade 4 pulmonary event — relevant given her bilateral infiltrative lung disease and altitude-shifted oximetry baseline.

toxicities.notes: possibly treatment-related; gemcitabine and docetaxel both carry pneumonitis risk

notes: The uLMS-specific first-line estimate for the fallback regimen: ORR 35.8%, mPFS 4.4 months — respectable but well short of LMS-04's 12.2-month PFS. Single-arm, n=42; no comparator.

intervention_label: Trabectedin vs dacarbazine after anthracycline failure (ET743-SAR-3007)

toxicities.notes: trabectedin arm only; class signal to watch during maintenance
sepsis/septic shock x3, rhabdomyolysis/sepsis, renal failure, renal failure/cardiac arrest, multiorgan failure

notes: Basis of the US trabectedin approval. For her it doubles as the single-agent safety dossier for the drug she will carry through LMS-04 maintenance — the hepatotoxicity and rhabdomyolysis rows are the ones her team will monitor. AE data from PMC full text (PMC5070559).

indication: metastatic non-adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma after standard chemotherapy
population_detail: angiogenesis-inhibitor-naive, prior anthracycline required; LMS was the largest histology; uterine sarcoma subset analyzed separately (Benson 2016 row)

indication: advanced uterine sarcoma (88.6% uLMS) within two prospective EORTC trials

intervention_label: Eribulin vs dacarbazine — leiomyosarcoma subgroup of Study 309

safety_summary: Grade >=3 TEAEs 69% (eribulin) vs 59% (dacarbazine) in the LMS subset; profiles manageable and consistent with the parent trial.

intervention_dose: olaparib 200 mg PO BID d1-7 + temozolomide 75 mg/m2 PO daily d1-7, q21d

one each for neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, rash

Toxicities empty after the fallback chain failed: abstract has no per-term data, no PMC deposit, Europe PMC subscription-only, Wiley page returns 402, and no trial registration is given in the abstract to reach a CT.gov AE tab.

Entirely retrospective and surgeon-selected: the 5-year figures describe patients healthy and oligometastatic enough to be operated on, not bilateral infiltrative disease like hers unless induction converts it.

intervention_label: Repeated pulmonary metastasectomy for leiomyosarcoma (Brigham series)
indication: pulmonary metastases from sarcoma; LMS subset analyzed (31/82)
population_detail: single-institution 1989-2004; LMS patients were mostly women (77%), had fewer lesions (mean 1.9) and 48% underwent repeat metastasectomy

outcome: median OS, LMS vs non-LMS metastasectomy

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: disease-free interval from primary resection to lung metastasis, and from metastasectomy to second recurrence, were the independent survival predictors in multivariate analysis

safety_summary: Surgical complications not reported in the abstract.
notes: Why the consulting oncologist keeps surgery on the table: resected LMS lung metastases can run an indolent course, and repeat resection is compatible with long survival. n=31 LMS at one hospital, all selected for operability — her bilateral infiltrative pattern is exactly what these series screen out, so this is a best-case ceiling, not an expectation.

indication: oligometastatic sarcoma lung metastases
population_detail: 44 patients / 56 lesions; 82% prior chemotherapy, 66% prior pulmonary resection; median lesion 2.0 cm
design: retrospective two-institution cohort
safety_summary: No grade >=3 events: three grade 2 chest-wall toxicities and one grade 2 pneumonitis in 44 patients.
notes: Largest multi-institution SBRT series in sarcoma lung metastases: excellent lesion-level control, low toxicity, but OS tracks systemic disease. Local control is not survival, and candidacy assumes discrete targetable lesions — her infiltrative pattern and 8,500-ft pulmonary baseline are both open questions for this modality.

Her interval is measured from an unrecognised resected primary, an unusual variant of that variable, and her young age and (assumed) ECOG 1 sit on the favorable side of the same model.

exclusion_reason: Letter commenting on the LMS-04 trial, not the trial report. Logged because this PMID commonly surfaces in searches for the regimen; the primary publication is PMID 35835135.

Olaratumab targets PDGFR-alpha, which is not one of her nominated targetable features, and the drug's STS indication was withdrawn after this negative confirmatory trial. Reviewed for its doxorubicin-control benchmark: median OS 21.9 months in the LMS stratum with modern supportive care.
notes: Kept out of synthesis per the mechanism-scope rule; the control-arm OS is context for interpreting single-agent doxorubicin expectations, nothing more.

exclusion_reason: Liposarcoma subgroup analysis of eribulin Study 309 — wrong histology for this uLMS case; it is the basis of the liposarcoma-only FDA label. Her histology is covered by the LMS subgroup row (PMID 31065111).
